title: The 2023 XMM-Newton X-ray dip of ASASSN-14ko is grey from 0.2 to 4.5 keV: the nucleus switches off in 1.4 d with no cold-absorption change, and slow 2021 onsets remove only soft flux
abstract: Question: campaign studies use the deep soft X-ray dip of the repeating nuclear transient ASASSN-14ko as a constant-period orbital clock (2020-2024), but no study tested what the dip is. Is it cold absorption by returning debris, or does the X-ray source disappear? Approach: we fitted the unused EPIC-pn pipeline spectra of the daily 2023 XMM-Newton campaign (27 observations) and its five-band time series without HEASoft or SAS (forward folding, W-statistic), and measured band colours of five clean Swift XRT dips (2020-2024) and of the NICER dip onsets of 2021. Results: in the 2023 ingress, all bands from 0.2 to 4.5 keV fall with one e-folding time of 0.5 d; normalised band levels divided by the 1-2 keV level are 0.974 +/- 0.016 (0.2-0.5 keV), 0.953 +/- 0.020 (0.5-1 keV) and 1.08 +/- 0.04 (2-4.5 keV). Any uniform change of cold column is below 7e19 cm^-2. A cold absorber is worse than grey scaling by delta W = 389 and 1257 in the two bright ingress spectra. The flux above the floor falls from 80 to 5 percent in 1.4 d (rest frame) and stays at the floor for at least 32 d; the floor keeps less than 0.04 percent of the soft excess. In all five XRT dips the 2-10 keV flux falls as much as the 0.3-2 keV flux. In contrast, the slow NICER onsets of 2021 (cycles 23 and 24) remove soft flux only: removed (1-2 keV)/(0.3-1 keV) = 0.085 and 0.32, with no 2-4 keV flux. Interpretation: the deep suppression is an achromatic switch-off of the whole X-ray continuum (intrinsic, or an opaque screen with Thomson depth of at least 3.9), not a debris column; the wandering onset is a separate soft component. Only the switch-off is a valid clock, and its trigger stays locked to the orbit within 0.5 d. Limitations: one resolved XMM-Newton ingress; pipeline products and canned responses; a phenomenological floor; windows set after inspection; intrinsic switch-off and opaque screen are not separated.
